idiom_name: plain class or dataclass screen state with explicit callbacks (tkinter Variable.trace_add where tkinter is used)
implementation_notes: The model is a plain class - frequently a dataclass - holding the screen state, with properties for derived display decisions and methods for commands; it imports no GUI package, so pytest drives it directly. No standard-library binding exists, so synchronization is explicit: the view calls a method and re-reads, or the model keeps a list of zero-argument callbacks. Where tkinter is the toolkit, its Variable classes carry individual widget values and trace_add('write', ...) supplies a change callback, but those variables belong to the view layer; toolkit signals from PySide/PyQt play the same role. The classic observer base class is justified only when several views must attach and detach dynamically - otherwise a callback list is less machinery.
pitfalls: Mutable dataclass fields need field(default_factory=...): the decorator rejects a bare mutable default outright, and a shared default would be worse.
Tkinter widgets may only be touched from the thread running the event loop; worker threads must marshal updates instead of calling widget methods directly.
Callbacks held by the toolkit are strong references, and scheduled after() callbacks still fire after the widget is gone unless they are cancelled on teardown.
A callback that writes back into the model while it is notifying re-enters the notify loop; guard with a flag or defer the write.
